# Companion to merge_conflict_markers_blocked_workflow.txt, which shows the
# pre-commit finalize refusing to seal a revealed file that still holds conflict
# markers. That guard has two holes, and a rebase falls through both:
#
#   1. it lives in the pre-commit hook and is gated on repo.InMerge(), i.e. on
#      MERGE_HEAD - which git only writes for `git merge`, never for a rebase,
#      cherry-pick or stash pop;
#   2. `sesam seal` itself does not check at all, even though `sesam status`
#      knows perfectly well the file is conflicted.
#
# So after a rebase the markers get encrypted into the object without a word.
# This test pins the gap down; it should start failing once the check moves into
# the seal path.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp main.txt $TMPDIR/main.txt
cp topic.txt $TMPDIR/topic.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

cp $TMPDIR/main.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'main: change secret'

exec git checkout -b topic HEAD~1
cp $TMPDIR/topic.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change secret'

! exec git rebase master
grep '^<<<<<<< ' s

# Mark the object resolved and continue WITHOUT touching the markers. No
# pre-commit hook runs here, so nothing objects.
exec git add .sesam/objects/s.sesam
exec git -c core.editor=true rebase --continue

# sesam knows the file is still conflicted...
exec sesam status
stdout 'conflicted'

# ...but seal encrypts the markers anyway, silently.
exec sesam seal
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout '<<<<<<< '
stdout '>>>>>>> '

# And the result verifies: the object is a perfectly well-formed, correctly
# signed secret. It just contains garbage.
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

-- base.txt --
line one
line two
line three
-- main.txt --
line one
MAIN
line three
-- topic.txt --
line one
TOPIC
line three
